messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Spanish, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (locked) | Target Requirement (Spanish) | |-------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------| | Ahi | Exclamation of emotional intensity | **¡Ay!** – interjection, no inflection. *Back‑translation check:* “Ah!” | | quanto | Marks degree of difficulty (“how”) | **cuán** + adjective (see *dura*) – adverbial interrogative, placed before the adjective. *Back‑translation check:* “how” | | a | Introduces infinitive purpose | **a** – preposition required before infinitive **decir**. *Back‑translation check:* “to” | | dir | Action the speaker wishes to perform | **decir** – infinitive, transitive verb. *Back‑translation check:* “to tell” | | qual | Refers to the unknown identity of X | **qué** – interrogative pronoun, neuter, object of **decir**. *Back‑translation check:* “what” | | era | Past state of X (the forest) | **era** – imperfect indicative of **ser**, 3ª sg., agrees with **qué**. *Back‑translation check:* “was” | | è | Present state of X as a “hard thing” | **es** – present indicative of **ser**, 3ª sg., links subject **cosa** to predicate **difícil**. *Back‑translation check:* “is” | | cosa | The entity being described (X) | **cosa** – feminine singular noun, subject complement of **es**. *Back‑translation check:* “thing” | | dura | Property indicating difficulty of description | **difícil** – adjective, feminine singular, predicative, agrees with **cosa**. Order with **quanto**: **cuán difícil**. *Back‑translation check:* “hard” | | esta | Points to the specific forest | **esta** – demonstrative adjective, feminine singular, agrees with **selva**. *Back‑translation check:* “this” | | selva | The referent X (forest) | **selva** – feminine singular noun, head of NP. *Back‑translation check:* “forest / wood” | | selvaggia | Property of X (wild) | **salvaje** – adjective, feminine singular, agrees with **selva**. *Back‑translation check:* “wild” | | e | Links adjectives | **y** – coordinating conjunction, no inflection. *Back‑translation check:* “and” | | aspra | Property of X (rough) | **áspera** – adjective, feminine singular, agrees with **selva**. *Back‑translation check:* “rough” | | e | Links adjectives | **y** – coordinating conjunction. *Back‑translation check:* “and” | | forte | Property of X (dense / strong) | **densa** (or **fuerte**) – adjective, feminine singular, agrees with **selva**; choose **densa** for “dense”. *Back‑translation check:* “strong / dense” | | che | Refers back to *selva* (X) | **que** – relative pronoun, introduces relative clause, agrees with antecedent **selva**. *Back‑translation check:* “which / that” | | nel | Locates the mental activity | **en el** – preposition **en** + masculine singular article **el** (contracted to **en el**). *Back‑translation check:* “in the” | | pensier | The mental arena where X is considered | **pensamiento** – masculine singular noun, object of preposition **en el**. *Back‑translation check:* “thought / mind” | | rinova | Causes the state of fear to re‑appear | **renueva** – present indicative, 3ª sg., agrees with subject **que** (referring to **selva**). *Back‑translation check:* “renews” | | la | Specifies the fear being spoken of | **el** – definite article, masculine singular, agrees with **miedo**. *Back‑translation check:* “the” | | paura | Emotional response evoked by X | **miedo** – masculine singular noun, direct object of **renueva**. *Back‑translation check:* “fear” | | ! | Marks exclamation, heightening affect | **¡** and **!** – opening and closing exclamation marks required in Spanish. *Back‑translation check:* punctuation unchanged |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 4: Ay cuán difícil es decir qué era / Ay cuán difícil resulta decir qué era / Ay cuán difícil resulta decir cuál era - Line 5: esta selva salvaje y áspera y densa / esta selva salvaje áspera y densa / esta selva salvaje y densa y áspera - Line 6: que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo / que al pensar renueva el miedo / que al recordarlo renueva el miedo

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Spanish lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura **Line Inventory:** - Ay cuán difícil es decir qué era **Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology needed; the phrase already contains the required interjection, comparative “cuán difícil”, and infinitival clause. **Target Text:** Ay cuán difícil es decir qué era
---
**Source Line:** 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte **Line Inventory:** - esta selva salvaje y áspera y densa **Assembly Notes:** - No extra elements required; the phrase supplies the demonstrative, noun, and three coordinated adjectives. **Target Text:** esta selva salvaje y áspera y densa
---
**Source Line:** 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! **Line Inventory:** - que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo! **Assembly Notes:** - No extra function‑words needed; the relative pronoun “que” introduces the clause, and the phrase ends with the required exclamation mark. **Target Text:** que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #4 Target Text: Ay cuán difícil es decir qué era Back-Translation: Ah how difficult it is to say what it was Reference Translation: Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what this wild and rough and dense wood was, which in thought renews the fear! Checks: End Punct <OK> | Coverage <OK> | Meaning Drift <OK> | Comparative Orientation <OK> | Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text:
- Line #5 Target Text: esta selva salvaje y áspera y densa Back-Translation: this wild and rough and dense forest Reference Translation: Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what this wild and rough and dense wood was, which in thought renews the fear! Checks: End Punct <OK> | Coverage <OK> | Meaning Drift <OK> | Comparative Orientation <N/A> | Hallucination <OK> Corrected Target Text:
- Line #6 Target Text: que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo! Back-Translation: which in thought renews the fear! Reference Translation: Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what this wild and rough and dense wood was, which in thought renews the fear!
